basis: MEASURED from the landed primary packets under reviews/, each read by exact path and re-digested against its own receipt. No orchestrator judgement enters the row classes.
contract_source: corrective_rereview_contract.v1.yaml, mesh_structure_r3.round_shapes.peer: scoped to challenged rows plus about a ten percent sample of supported rows, one peer agent per about two clusters
grouping_note: The contract keys the peer round to CLUSTER PAIRS, not to parts. Eleven peers falls out of 22 clusters either way, but the grouping differs and the cluster-pair grouping is the one the contract states.
open_question_for_the_controlling_agent: The contract permits SAMPLING about ten percent of supported rows at the peer round. Ezekiel is on the OW-6b hard-book track, whose primaries ran at FULL coverage with no sampling. Whether a hard-track book may sample its both-support rows at peer, or must cover them all, is not the orchestrator's call and is NOT decided here. This file therefore marks peer_required_by_contract on every non-both-support row and leaves the both-support rows unsampled, so either ruling can be applied without recomputing.

DISAGREE_STANCE rows are the strongest peer targets on the evidence, but the contract does not name that class explicitly. Whether they get a heavier treatment than other challenged rows is a scope decision, not a measurement.
honest_limits: A row's class describes what the two packets SAY, not which lane is right. Nothing here adjudicates any finding.

Both lanes are Anthropic-family models, so agreement between them is corroboration from a correlated voice and never independent confirmation. A BOTH_SUPPORT class is therefore a weaker signal than its name suggests.
SINGLE_LANE rows exist only while clusters are in flight and will reclassify on landing; re-run this builder after the last packet lands.
